plain_definition: A listing category some US national securities exchanges, including Cboe BZX and NYSE Arca, use in their own rulebooks for exchange-traded products structured as a trust holding a commodity -- including, for many recent filings, bitcoin or another crypto asset -- rather than as a registered investment company. Nasdaq uses a similarly-purposed but differently-numbered rule for the same kind of product. Each such listing originally required its own individual, SEC-approved rule change; the SEC later adopted generic listing standards letting qualifying products list without that bespoke filing.
formal_definition: E.g. Cboe BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4) and NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Commodity-Based Trust Shares); Nasdaq's parallel category is Rule 5711(d). Shares in this category are registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and, per issuers' own SEC-filed disclosure, are not registered investment companies under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
